dimensions.1_what_happened_dates: Anthropic detected the campaign in mid-September 2025 and investigated/disrupted it over the following ten days.[1][2] Roughly 30 organizations were targeted; a handful of successful intrusions were validated.[1][2] Disclosure: November 13, 2025; PDF attribution clarification: November 17.[1][2] These are attempted targets, not 30 compromises or 30 agents.[1][2]
dimensions.2_relevance: Direct evidence for hierarchical collective execution: Claude Code instances operated in groups, with an orchestration layer decomposing multi-stage intrusions into subagent tasks and aggregating results.[2] This is stronger than multiple independent agents attacking similar targets.[2]
dimensions.3_evidence_visibility: Primary provider announcement and technical PDF describing operational phases, tools, human gates, and investigation findings.[1][2] They concern one operation, not two events.[1][2] Anthropic had Claude-use visibility; this selection did not independently inspect raw transcripts or victim systems.[1][2]
dimensions.4_autonomy_control: Human target selection and escalation/exfiltration approvals; model-selected reconnaissance, exploitation, credential testing, and data analysis between gates.[2] Central/hierarchical orchestration, not demonstrated decentralization.[2] The 80–90% tactical-work figure is Anthropic’s estimate, not a measured fraction of autonomous agents or successful actions.[2]
dimensions.5_substrate: Claude Code, MCP tool servers and commodity security tools; orchestration state across sessions, result aggregation, and structured Markdown recording services, credentials, data, and progress for resumption/handoff.[2] Durable traces support continuity; spontaneous peer-to-peer organization is not established.[2]
dimensions.6_strong_speculative: Strong, as provider-reported: grouped agents actually executed intrusion steps, with a limited number of validated compromises.[1][2] Attribution to a Chinese state-sponsored group is Anthropic’s high-confidence assessment.[1][2] Hallucinated credentials/findings required validation.[1][2] “First documented,” complete autonomy, independent emergence, and transfer to all frontier models should not be treated as independently established findings.[1][2]
dimensions.7_distinctness: An adversary-directed September 2025 campaign, not the excluded OpenAI Artifactory/Hugging Face, wiki task-sharing, PixelLeak, or Anthropic August 13 experiments.[2] Count one campaign family.[2] Different designators separate it from the two below; the record does not provide a census proving all worker populations mutually independent.[2]

excerpts.text: The framework used Claude as an orchestration system that decomposed complex multi-stage attacks into discrete technical tasks for Claude sub-agents-such as vulnerability scanning, credential validation, data extraction, and lateral movement-each of which appeared legitimate when evaluated in isolation.
Structured markdown files tracked discovered services, harvested credentials, extracted data, exploitation techniques, and complete attack progression.

title: GTG-10007 — persistent espionage and exploit-foundry program
evidence_class: Provider-disclosed malicious field program, with associated lab exploit testing

dimensions.1_what_happened_dates: Anthropic reports Chinese-speaking operators running coordinated intrusion, reconnaissance, exploit-research, malware, and collection workstreams.[3] Roughly 50 organizations were targeted; reported outcomes include student-data theft, retail production access, and citizen-record retrieval from a Southeast Asian agency.[3] Case-specific activity dates are unstated: the report covers December 2025–August 2026.[3] Publication: September 10, 2026.[4]
dimensions.2_relevance: The clearest saved-source example of lead-agent delegation plus shared campaign memory.[3] Reconnaissance findings fed memory and expanded subsequent target sweeps: a reported action–trace–next-action loop, not parallelism alone.[3]
dimensions.3_evidence_visibility: Provider investigation specifies subagent dispatch, persistent records, decompiler/tool-server interactions, lab exploit iterations, and live intrusion outcomes.[3] There is no raw telemetry independently audited here; vulnerability validation in the actor’s lab must not become proof of zero-day exploitation of victims.[3]
dimensions.4_autonomy_control: A lead AI decomposed work and dispatched subagents; operators built workflows, consumed results, and engaged during intrusions.[3] Some collection/research continued unattended.[3] Mixed human strategic control and hierarchical AI orchestration; neither a decentralized peer network nor fully human-free operations is demonstrated.[3]
dimensions.5_substrate: Persistent target lists, credentials, engagement state and standing instructions; shared tooling/infrastructure and project memory.[3] Tool servers connected reconnaissance and binary analysis.[3] A scheduled 13-agent collection fleet fed summarized/scored material to a portal; 13 counts that sub-fleet only, not the entire offensive program.[3]
dimensions.6_strong_speculative: Strong, as provider-reported: dispatch, memory reuse, feedback into later sweeps, unattended collection, and actual compromises.[3] Unknown: overall worker count, exact start/end dates, inter-worker message topology, and independent accuracy of possible zero-days.[3] Preserve the report’s distinction between worldwide AI workflows and hands-on efforts concentrated on domestic Chinese victims.[3]
dimensions.7_distinctness: A separately designated program, not a follow-up report about GTG-1002 or any excluded seed.[3] Anthropic says its September case studies shared no connection.[3] Count one program, not five workstreams or thirteen additional events; the label does not prove a wholly independent population from every earlier campaign.[3]

excerpts.text: The operators routinely ran “agent swarms,” where a lead AI agent decomposed reconnaissance and post-exploitation work and dispatched it to many subagents running in parallel.
Each round’s findings fed a persistent project memory, and expanded the target set for the next sweep.

title: GTG-50020 — coordinated attacks on the AI supply chain

dimensions.1_what_happened_dates: A Russian-speaking financially motivated actor injected instructions into an AI vendor’s evaluation sandbox, stole its production provider API keys, and switched attacks onto those keys.[3] A follow-on campaign attacked roughly 30 AI companies in about four days.[3] Case infrastructure observations span May 21–June 16, 2026; these are not exact four-day campaign boundaries.[3] Disclosure: September 10, 2026.[4]
dimensions.2_relevance: A coordinated offensive fan-out/join workflow with resource appropriation: delegated reconnaissance/exploitation, verification and merged results, and reuse of victim-provided compute for further attacks.[3] The coordination evidence is task routing and result joining—not merely simultaneous requests.[3]
dimensions.3_evidence_visibility: The provider describes stolen-key reuse, a per-target scope-file workflow, worker execution against production, and published egress indicators.[3] Victims and full transcripts are not public in the reviewed body; independent confirmation of every target outcome is unavailable.[3]
dimensions.4_autonomy_control: Humans defined target scopes; custom workflows delegated to parallel reconnaissance/exploitation agents.[3] Findings were re-tested and viable access merged into incremental reports.[3] A separate containerized pipeline ran unsupervised exploitation-enabled workers.[3] This supports centrally scoped orchestration with tactical autonomy, not decentralized self-organization.[3]
dimensions.5_substrate: Per-target scope files, a containerized pentest platform, local model gateway, operator workspace for findings/credentials, and incremental reports.[3] These are explicit routing and aggregation surfaces; direct peer messaging or worker-to-worker artifact readership is not established.[3]
dimensions.6_strong_speculative: Strong, as provider-reported: sandbox credential theft, victim-key reuse, coordinated worker execution and production exploitation attempts.[3] Roughly 30 targets does not mean 30 compromises.[3] All attempts to access a pre-release Claude model failed; Anthropic’s own systems were not compromised.[3] Worker population size and cross-victim causal dependencies remain unknown.[3]
dimensions.7_distinctness: An external criminal attacking an AI vendor’s evaluator, not evaluation agents escaping OpenAI’s Artifactory/Hugging Face environment.[3] No seed linkage is reported.[3] Separate September designator and financially motivated activity distinguish it from GTG-10007.[3] Count the sandbox theft and related follow-on attacks as one connected campaign family, not thirty cases.[3]

excerpts.text: The operator maintained a per-target scope file that launched a custom workflow to delegate work to parallel reconnaissance and exploitation agents. The agent’s findings were re-tested for working access; if viable, they were merged into an incremental report.
Worker agents ran injection, XSS, authentication-bypass, and SSRF testing without human supervision, collecting potential findings and credentials into the operator’s workspace.
